title: Fit the blue suction-cup tool to a robot's manual quick-change flange and lock it on
instruction: Fit the blue suction-cup tool to the tool flange on the wrist stand and lock it on, leaving the gripper tool in the rack. Then let go of everything, with the tool hanging locked on the flange, and take both arms back to where they started.
context: Robot cells swap end effectors (grippers, suction cups, welding torches) on quick-change tool changers. When the people who build, commission or re-tool a robot cell fit a tool by hand on a manual changer, the tool's plate has to be held up square on the flange's two locating dowels while a locking ring or lever is worked; let go too early and the tool drops, damaging it or the fixture. One hand holds the tool, the other works the lock. The real trial uses an inert wrist stand in place of a robot arm, with the same changer at the same pose.
setup: A table in front of two arms (bases 61 cm apart), seen by one overhead camera and a camera on each wrist. Distances are measured forward from the line between the arm bases and sideways from the midpoint between them. (1) An inert wrist stand in place of a parked robot's wrist: a plywood board 20 x 18 x 1.8 cm (25 to 45 cm forward, 4 to 22 cm left of the centre line) held to the table by two C-clamps on its far edge, and bolted to it a grey printed PETG pedestal carrying a dummy wrist 6.8 cm across, its axis 30 cm forward and 8.5 cm above the table, pointing right. Bolted to the wrist's face (ISO 9409-1-50-4-M6) is the robot side of a manual quick-change tool changer, its 7.4 cm mating face 2 cm left of the centre line, facing right. (2) A black PETG locking ring 8.8 cm across turning on the flange just behind its face, with three claws reaching 1.1 cm in front of the face, and an orange PETG lever reaching 11 cm toward the arms, then bending left to a pad 4.5 x 3 cm topped with black rubber (its middle 19 cm forward, 8.3 cm left of the centre line, its top 9.8 cm above the table at rest, with a small lip on its near end). Ring and lever weigh 140 g. Pressing the pad down turns the ring, up to 35 degrees (the pad then 6.6 cm lower); friction (0.12 N m) keeps it where it is left, and the lever's weight (0.04 N m) helps it down. (3) A grey printed tool rack right of the centre line with two slots, each tool lying left-right with its plate facing the flange: a blue suction-cup tool (120 g: printed PETG with a steel ballast bar inside; a plate 6 cm across, its face 30 cm forward and 12 cm right of the centre line; a body 4.4 cm across ending in a black suction cup 22.5 cm right of the centre line), and a grey two-finger gripper tool (140 g), the same but 18 cm forward. Each tool has a square black handle 1.6 cm across on top, 5 cm from its plate's face, its top 14 cm above the table. A tool is seated when both dowels are in its bushings in a pose the full-size parts allow: for each dowel, with its tip d mm past the plate's face, its axis e mm off the bushing's there and tilted t, e + d tan t + 3 (1/cos t - 1) <= 0.005 + max(0, 1.5 - d) mm (README); its lug fronts within 10 mm of the face; to go on, its lugs between the lips. A tool seated with the ring within 8 degrees of open is taken as the ring passes 8 degrees (drawn home onto the face, square) and locked from 25 degrees. Back below 25 it unlocks; within 8 degrees of open it comes free. A ring turned with no tool seated takes nothing. The changer, printed in PETG round bought precision parts (full sizes, drawings, STL files and part numbers in the README; angles seen facing the flange): the flange (a 74 mm lip in front of a 64 mm journal) is bolted to the wrist by four M6 screws on a 50 mm circle, through a 76 mm retaining disc behind the ring. Two 6 mm dowels stand 6 mm out of its face, 22 mm from the axis at 12 o'clock (round, ISO 2338 6 h8) and 6 o'clock (diamond, DIN 6321 form C), 44 mm apart. Six springs in the ring's front face press on the lip and hold the ring against the disc; a 4 mm pin in the disc, running in a groove in the ring's back, stops it at 1 degree past open and at 35 degrees. The ring's three claws (at 2, 6 and 10 o'clock with the ring open, each 80 degrees of arc) have lips 32 to 38 mm from the axis whose back faces are cams: a lead-in ramp from 9.0 to 3.6 mm in front of the face (ring turned 8 to 20 degrees), a clamp ramp to 2.8 mm (20 to 25 degrees) and a flat dwell. Each 8 mm tool plate has three 3 mm thick lugs at 12, 4 and 8 o'clock, each 24 degrees wide, from its rim to 36 mm from the axis, and two hardened bushings for the dowels (DIN 179, 6 mm F7 bores: 0.010-0.044 mm clearance on the round dowel) behind 1.5 x 45 degree lead-in chamfers. With the ring open the lugs pass through the 40-degree gaps between the lips; turned 25 degrees, the lips pull the plate onto the face with about 15 N.
scoring: Judged at the end of the trial. 0.0 if the gripper tool was ever locked on. Otherwise 1.0: the suction tool locked on (seated on the dowels with the ring open, taken as the ring passed 8 degrees, and the ring still turned 25 degrees or more), each gripper's fingertip centre (TCP) at least 4 cm from its handle and from the lever's pad, and both arms back where they started (each TCP within 5 cm of its start); 0.5: the suction tool locked on otherwise; 0.25: the suction tool seated on the dowels, with the ring open, at some point; else 0.0. The trial ends at the run limit, or once the full score has held for 1 s with the suction tool still. In a real trial, the same tiers are judged from the changer and the video: locked = at the end, the ring's index line is at or past the LOCK mark (25 degrees) on the retaining disc, a 0.2 mm feeler gauge does not enter between plate and face anywhere round the rim, and the tool hangs on the flange; seated with the ring open = both dowel tips in the plate's bushings (it no longer slides sideways) while the index line was inside the 8-degree mark; the gripper tool locked = the same test for it, at any time; hands clear and arms home = TCP distances from the arms' logged joint angles, as in the simulation.
reset_notes: Turn the ring back open, take the suction tool off and lay both tools back in the rack.
fidelity: Rigid-body PhysX (Isaac Sim 6.1, 20 Hz control) at real size and mass. Simplified: the stand is fixed; claws, lugs and dowels are drawn but do not touch. Seating checks the full-size dowels in the bushings (offset and tilt shrink with depth: 0.005 mm in the bore); stops 5.6 mm out hold a pushed plate with the dowel tips 0.4 mm into the chamfers. From 8 deg a fixed joint holds it home and square, with no play (real ramps draw it in by 20 deg); ring friction is a moved hinge spring.
